findings.notes: The subject/positive/negative/question chart replaces the rejected subject-to-be chain. Full and contracted negatives occupy their own visible lines. Usually and Now are separate labeled example columns. Text remains legible; all response fields fit.
Bag evidence and full too-small/not-big-enough versus big-enough sentence models remain meaningful and clear. No formula prose; correction rules have usable writing room.
Frequency counts use clear numbered circles and short labels. Complete Question/Answer models occupy separate columns. Task source days and blank Unit5QRreserve are readable and unobstructed.
All six spatial pictures retain useful scale and unambiguous labels; complete examples support meaning. Sources, empty rewrite rules and final open lines remain readable and inside the page.
The route map retains legible building labels and a clear starting orientation. Directions are actual imperative models; the controlled route information and response spaces are usable.
Opening-day facts, modal positive/negative/question forms and complete avoid/use examples are aligned in distinct tables. Can uses the base verb correctly. QRreserve and rewrite rows remain clear.
Yesterday/today facts, was/were form contrasts and full short answers occupy readable chart rows. Subject groups are explicit labels, not compressed rule chains. Both question-writing areas fit.
The three-day timeline makes ago concrete. Month/year/date columns contain complete preposition examples. No inline mapping chain remains; Unit7QRreserve is clear.

Past positive/negative/question forms, a be-question correction and regular-past spellings are compact aligned charts. No congested grammar prose remains. The diary source and controlled/freer response areas fit without crowding.

Four action images/captions remain whole enough to supply the task evidence. The verb/past table and full past-simple form chart are clear at print scale. All account, rewriting, question and open-writing lines remain available.

Should positive/negative/question models and full avoid/use examples make base-verb use explicit. The matching layout and rewrite fields are easy to follow; no compressed all-subject rule paragraph remains.
Have/has and singular/plural hurt(s) appear in two concise full-example charts. Task models, message frame, answer rules and Unit8QRreserve remain legible and clear.

overall_judgment: Pass. The changed grammar explanations use actual charts, aligned examples or task-serving physical evidence, with consistent ordinary text and clear response space. None of the rejected inline pronoun/form, contraction or rule chains was visible in these explanation areas.
review_scope_limit: Independent visual/editorial review of the specified final PDF pages; root owns whole-book structural, parity and publication checks.
